topic: Nanami's rule that sorcerers survive by making friends accept they might not come back traces to Haibara's loss, and Yuji inherits that exact rule after Shibuya
title: Nanami's Rule For Sorcerers Came From One Loss
description: Nanami Kento's whole philosophy about the job traces back to one person: his old classmate Yu Haibara. After Shibuya, Yuji Itadori ends up carrying the exact same rule Nanami once said he hated. From the full story: Nanami Was Never Supposed To Survive Shibuya.
comment: Is Nanami's rule about sorcerers wisdom, or just guilt he never got over? Pick one.

lines.text: Nanami's whole philosophy about sorcerers traces back to one lost friend.
His classmate Yu Haibara was endlessly optimistic, the one person who made missions feel lighter.

shot.fallback: smiling student in Jujutsu High uniform

lines.text: Then Haibara never made it back from a mission, and something in Nanami shut down completely.

shot.fallback: grieving swordsman standing in the rain

lines.text: Nanami walked away from being a sorcerer and spent years working an ordinary office job instead.
He admits it himself: he didn't quit. He ran.

shot.fallback: man walking alone down a city street

lines.text: And the reason he gives is brutal: sorcerers survive by making their friends accept they might not come back.

shot.fallback: swordsman speaking seriously to a student

lines.text: Carry that rule into Shibuya, because it's the exact rule Yuji inherits...

shot.fallback: swordsman walking toward a chaotic city street

lines.text: After Nanami's part in the story ends, Yuji breaks completely, for the first time in the whole arc.
Weeks later he makes a private promise: he'll carry Nanami's share of the suffering too.

shot.fallback: young fighter standing resolute after grief

lines.text: That's not a new rule. It's the same one, just handed down.

shot.fallback: young fighter carrying an invisible weight forward

lines.text: Because Nanami's whole philosophy about sorcerers...

shot.fallback: two students in Jujutsu High uniforms
